settings.name_in_paper: Federated bandit optimization with generic non-linear (parametric) objective
unmapped: N clients interact round-robin with a shared function for T rounds each (NT total interactions), star-shaped communication via a server; communication cost is also measured
Parametric class f_w with w in [0,1]^{d_w}, domain X subset [0,1]^{d_x}; bounded |f|<=F, gradient bound C_g and Hessian bound C_h in w
Geometric conditions on expected squared loss L(w): (tau,gamma)-growth or local mu-strong convexity, dissipativity, local self-concordance
Learner uses knowledge of F, mu, d_w to set communication threshold
settings.definition_quote: In each round, $N$ clients interact with the unknown function $f$ in a round-robin manner, for a total number of $T$ rounds ... $y_{t}=f(\bx_{t}) + \eta_{t}$ ... $\eta_{t}$ is independent, zero-mean, $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian noise ... $R_{NT}=\sum_{t=1}^{NT} f(\bx^*) - f(\bx_t)$

bound.regime: T >= C d_w^2 F^4 iota^2 / N * max{mu^{gamma/(2-gamma)}/tau^{2/(2-gamma)}, zeta/(mu c^2)}^2

symbols.d_w: parameter dimension of the function class
symbols.mu_sc: local strong convexity parameter mu of the expected loss L(w) at w*

conditions: Assumptions 1-3: realizability, bounded/smooth function approximation, growth/local strong convexity, dissipativity, local self-concordance
T lower bound as in regime

source.label: thm:regret_communication
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg:fed_go_ucb} with parameters $T_{0}=\sqrt{NT}$, $\lambda=C_{\lambda}\sqrt{NT}$, $\gamma=\frac{d_{w} F^{4} T}{\mu^{2}N}$, and $\epsilon \leq \frac{8}{C \sqrt{NT}}$, has cumulative regret $R = \tilde{O}(\sqrt{NT}F + \sqrt{NT} d_{w}^{3}F^{4}/\mu^{2} + N d_{w}^{4}F^{4}/\mu^{2})$ with probability at least $1-\delta$

results.notes: Regret over NT total interactions (Phase I + Phase II). Regret is the realized sum f(x*)-f(x_t) bounded w.p. 1-delta.

bound.regime: same T lower bound as Theorem 5

source.label: thm:regret_communication
source.quote: and communication cost $C_{\text{phase I + phase II}} = \tilde{O}(N^{1.5} \sqrt{T}d_{w}d_{x}\exp{(d_{x})}+N^{1.5} d_{w}^{2}\mu/F^{2} )$.

results.notes: Communication cost = total number of real numbers transferred. Probability qualifier not explicitly attached to communication cost in the statement; treated as part of the same high-probability theorem.
